a4202.speaker: Abdiaziz Osman Mohamed, Deputy Head of Social Affairs for Banaadir
a4202.speech: “This win comes from the team’s good play, good training, high discipline, and better coordination. We congratulate the players, coaches, and our fans. It is a result of months of commitment.”

a4202.speaker: Saadiya Ali, MCC supporter
a4202.speech: “I’ve supported MCC since childhood because my late father worked for the Mogadishu Municipal Council. I dedicate the win to him,” she told local media.

a5154.speaker: Research by Kuziemko and Werner (2006)
a5154.speech: found that countries serving as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council receive more foreign aid from the UN and US-led agencies like UNICEF during their tenure.

a5214.speaker: Mohamed Ali Nafti, Tunisia's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Migration and Tunisians Abroad, and Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister
a5214.speech: Have reaffirmed the necessity of close coordination among Arab and Muslim countries; in a phone conversation on Monday they discussed the worsening humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip, border closures, and the potential repercussions of the Israel-Iran escalation on regional stability, and both advocated for collective diplomatic action aimed at anticipating security risks and promoting sustainable political solutions.

a5214.speaker: Mohamed Ali Nafti, Tunisia's Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister
a5214.speech: Highlighted the strength of bilateral ties between Tunisia and Egypt, calling for enhanced cooperation across multiple sectors of mutual interest, and agreed to continue consultations ahead of upcoming bilateral meetings scheduled in the coming weeks.

a5214.speaker: Al Soumoud humanitarian caravan coordination
a5214.speech: Announced its return to Tunisia on Monday after being denied passage permits by Egyptian and Libyan authorities.

a5214.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Foreign Minister
a5214.speech: Reiterated ongoing efforts in Cairo to achieve a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas and to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance.

a5308.speaker: OneStep Trading (Pty) Ltd, operators of the Food Lovers Market franchise at Gateway Mall in Lilongwe
a5308.speech: Announced its closure due to severe foreign exchange shortages and declining consumer disposable income, citing significant financial losses as a key reason for winding down operations.

a5308.speaker: Malawi Confederation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MCCCI)
a5308.speech: Has highlighted that the forex shortage is causing the private sector to "slowly die," with businesses unable to sustain operations under the current economic conditions.

a5308.speaker: World Bank
a5308.speech: Has repeatedly warned that without urgent macroeconomic reforms, Malawi's economic stability is at serious risk.

a5327.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) report
a5327.speech: States that “the number of people in a situation of acute food insecurity and in need of urgent assistance (…) could increase from 2.79 million to around 3.28 million people, from October [2024] to March, 2025”; with data from 63 districts among those most affected by climate shocks, 773,000 people are also expected to face an “emergency” situation in the country ; “This could happen as a result of the depletion of food reserves and the impact of armed groups in Cabo Delgado and parts of Nampula and Niassa, as well as the effects of La Niña (…), mainly in the south and centre of the country” ; the districts of Macomia and Quissanga, among those most affected by terrorist attacks, the intensification of the conflict and the limitations on access for humanitarian assistance could lead to an “emergency” situation.

a5327.speaker: Index created by the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO)
a5327.speech: Indicates that all provinces in the country will be affected, but with the emphasis on Gaza, Inhambane, Manica, Tete, as well as Cabo Delgado.

a5327.speaker: United Nations
a5327.speech: Estimates that food insecurity aggravated by El Niño has reached “unprecedented levels” in Mozambique, threatening almost five million people, in a scenario of drought and a lack of international funding for support on the ground.

a5327.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) report
a5327.speech: The conclusions resulting from the analysis of agricultural activity and food insecurity indicate that “it has reached unprecedented levels in Mozambique”, with a total of 4,890,232 people threatened by this food insecurity by the end of the current agricultural campaign in March, 2025; in 2024 the agency launched an appeal for US$222 million (€213 million) in international support to combat the effects of the drought in Mozambique, but acknowledges that it faces “a significant funding gap”, having raised only US$28.7 million (€27.5 million), equivalent to 13% of the identified needs.

a5510.speaker: Chinese authorities / Maritime Safety Administration of China (statement)
a5510.speech: Announced today that live-fire military exercises will be carried out in the Bohai Sea, between the Chinese coast and the Korean peninsula, between 29 and 30 October; according to the statement published on the authority's official portal in Dalian, Liaoning province, access to the targeted zones will be restricted during the test period.

a5510.speaker: Beijing (Chinese government)
a5510.speech: Filed a formal complaint with the United States in 2020 over the overflight of a U-2 aircraft in an exclusion zone during military exercises.

a5642.speaker: Khaled Fadi Mahmoud El-Shazli, new Ambassador of Egypt to Djibouti
a5642.speech: Underlined the historic ties uniting the two countries, citing the strategic projects currently being finalised between Djibouti and Egypt and President Sisi’s willingness to formalise the opening of a direct air route between Cairo and Djibouti, to be the fruit of a partnership between Air Djibouti and Egyptian aviation, the launch of a branch of Banque Misr, and the establishment of a partnership on agricultural expertise ; Mentioned wanting to devote the essence of his mission in Djibouti to working towards fruitful partnerships in fisheries, communications and new technologies with the company benya.tech, in order to import a datacenter to support digitalisation and benefit Djibouti and its government, which are in pole position given the nine submarine cables serving the territory ; Expressed his commitment to developing a distinctive cooperation in the areas of health, logistics zones and roads.

a5642.speaker: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, Prime Minister of Djibouti
a5642.speech: Mentioned his wish to see agriculture developed on the bed of the Ambouli wadi, drawing inspiration from agricultural expertise on the Nile ; Welcomed Ambassador El-Shazli and expressed his support for him during his stay in Djibouti.

a5673.speaker: Annual Report of the African Water Facility, January – December 2022 (African Development Bank, June 2023)
a5673.speech: States that the African Water Facility recorded a performance judged “solid” at end-December 2022, with the financial position of the AWF Special Fund showing 14.29 million euros available to cover new commitments beyond 2022; that the Facility approached more than 20 potential donors last year to meet annual advocacy and resource-mobilisation targets and held consultations with donors in March 2022 at the 9th World Water Forum in Dakar, Senegal; that it had 26 active projects under which 5.12 million euros were disbursed in 2022, that 43 project concepts were reviewed and 20 judged fit for inclusion in the AWF project pipeline, ten projects fully appraised and eight approved for a grant; and that, boosted by the increase in technical staff, the Facility boldly moved to advance its programmes after the slowdown caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, with the NDF/Denmark water, sanitation and hygiene (Wash) programme in the Sahel and the Horn of Africa finally taking off.

a5673.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (pledge)
a5673.speech: Among the concrete pledges received was that of USAID for US$3 million in unrestricted contributions and technical assistance, to support the annual target of mobilising 14 million euros in new commitments.

a5723.speaker: Ramtane Lamamra, Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan
a5723.speech: Said on Thursday that it is time to put an end to the "heartbreaking suffering" in Sudan, and stressed that it is the collective responsibility of the international community to do everything in its power to end the heartbreaking suffering of Sudan, which has gone on for far too long. ; "It is heartbreaking to note that the ongoing conflict - for no less than 20 months now - continues to have a devastating impact on the Sudanese people, in particular on women and children" ; "this cannot go on any longer."

a5723.speaker: Ramtane Lamamra, Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for Sudan (quoted in a press release)
a5723.speech: Stressed that the partnership between multilateral organisations and the main peacemakers remains indispensable: "I am convinced that we will continue to build on these gains, ensuring the complementarity, coherence and coordination of our efforts on behalf of Sudan and its people."

a5723.speaker: Participants of the third consultative meeting on Sudan (final communiqué)
a5723.speech: Insisted on the urgent need to reach a ceasefire in Sudan in order to establish peace and stability in the country, urging the warring parties to fully respect their obligations under international humanitarian law as well as their commitments under the Jeddah declaration; also reaffirmed their intention to strengthen coordination and step up efforts, ensuring that the various initiatives aimed at ending the war in Sudan and at resuming an inclusive political process are complementary.

a5723.speaker: Civilians who fled the war in Sudan for Uganda (testimony to UN investigators)
a5723.speech: Gave "poignant" testimony to UN investigators, detailing the abuses of the deadly conflict raging in Sudan; the mission collected poignant testimony of massive destruction, killings, rapes and other sexual violence.

a5723.speaker: United Nations Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan
a5723.speech: Its members expressed their concern at the worsening impact of the conflict on civilians after meeting some 200 Sudanese refugees during a visit to Uganda from 1 to 18 December.

a5723.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, chair of the UN fact-finding mission on Sudan
a5723.speech: "Instead of contributing positively to the reconstruction of Sudan, millions of Sudanese refugees are trapped in dire conditions in camps and settlements in neighbouring countries while the conflict rages."

a5723.speaker: Sudanese refugees who fled Gezira State
a5723.speech: Described rapes, forced labour and other serious violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, perpetrated largely by the RSF.

a5723.speaker: Sudanese refugee women interviewed by the UN mission
a5723.speech: Several women highlighted the increase in the number of miscarriages, while others said they were disproportionately affected by air strikes or shelling on markets, both as vendors and when buying essential goods for their families; the women also reported sexual harassment, in particular from individuals wearing RSF uniforms and speaking foreign languages, and many expressed their desire to shape the future of Sudan and not to leave the country's future in the hands of the men at war.

a5723.speaker: Mona Rishmawi, member of the UN fact-finding mission on Sudan
a5723.speech: "Sudan's women and children are not only the main victims of this senseless conflict, but they also hold the key to a peaceful and dignified life for all Sudanese."

a5776.speaker: Mmusi Kgafela, Botswana Trade and Industry Minister
a5776.speech: Said the EU-SADC EPA support programme was officially launched in 2021 and will run until July 2024: “The EU-Botswana Business Forum was born out of this support programme,” he said when welcoming delegates to the four-day event.

a5776.speaker: Mmusi Kgafela, Botswana Trade and Industry Minister
a5776.speech: Said “We are optimistic that we will be able to present compelling, value propositions to EU companies that have graced the Business Forum and Global Expo,” adding that Botswana is ready to receive Foreign Direct Investment from Europe and across the world, and is hoping that during the Business Forum and Expo there will be long-term investments and partnership deals.

a5776.speaker: Mmusi Kgafela, Botswana Trade and Industry Minister
a5776.speech: Said that in 2022 Belgium was the only European country in the list of top export destinations for Botswana, with trade accounting for 18.7 percent of total exports, the main product being diamonds: “On the investment side, Europe remains the key partner for Botswana and in 2021, Europe accounted for 57.1 percent of stock of FDI of which mainland Europe contributed 47.9 percent,” further assuring European investors that Botswana has a favourable investment climate with the highest credit rating in Africa of BBB+ from Standard and Poor’s and an A3 rating from Moody’s Investor Services.

a5776.speaker: Mmusi Kgafela, Botswana Trade and Industry Minister
a5776.speech: Told delegates that Botswana continues to improve the business environment to align it to private sector needs: “Seriously consider investing in Botswana. Take advantage of the opportunities presented by the many trade agreements Botswana is a party to, including the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). This is tempting because it covers the whole of Africa,” adding that Botswana avails herself as the launch-pad of the AfCFTA market and beyond.

a5776.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a5776.speech: Said the Business Forum and Expo comes after the successful hosting of the 15th US-Africa Summit hosted in Botswana in partnership with the Corporate Council on Africa, and that these efforts demonstrate Botswana’s aspirations to transform into a regional hub for investment and international trade as well as MICE; said Botswana is intentional to maximise on opportunities presented by positive bilateral and multilateral relations to broaden key socio-economic developmental areas such as education, health, finance and other priority sectors.

a5776.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a5776.speech: Said the African Union has declared 2023 as the year of ‘Accelerating the Implementation of the AfCFTA’, following ratification by close to 90 percent of all AU Member States: “It is befitting that the theme of this year’s Global Expo Botswana resonates with the continental declaration. The main aim of the declaration is to create a single African market for goods and services, and further promote economic integration and development across the continent in line with the continental flagship project of Agenda 2063,” adding that the Global Expo platform offers prospects for strong future bilateral as well as continental partnerships: “Such partnerships, if properly harnessed, stand to be very instrumental in addressing the critical shortages we face regarding specific economic enablers for the movement of goods and services.”

a5776.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a5776.speech: Believes that the economic enablers of interest for sustainable economic development include suitable road networks, railway lines, airports as well as the necessary digital infrastructure: “What is critical at this point, is for our Governments, Botswana included, to align all the institutional machinery we have available; progressively rationalise all policies and strategies of development, or develop new ones; the aim being to nurture and favour this intended acceleration and transform Africa into the global powerhouse of the future that we all want,” and said that in Botswana government has already initiated a Transformational Agenda aimed at breaking current growth barriers, removing economic hurdles and building momentum towards high-income status by 2036.

a5776.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a5776.speech: Added that digitisation is not only an economic tool, but also a means of fostering active and responsible citizenship through availing various forms and sources of information, knowledge and do-it-yourself skills that engender self-efficacy and capacity for networking in community development initiatives.

a5880.speaker: Both delegations (U.S. and Nigeria, Binational Commission joint readout)
a5880.speech: Both sides acknowledged that the relationship is grounded in shared values of pluralism and respect for sovereignty, and renewed commitments to promote democracy and respect for human rights, cooperate for shared economic prosperity, and jointly overcome health and security challenges.

a5880.speaker: U.S. delegation
a5880.speech: Welcomed an overview of Foreign Minister Tuggar's 4D policy of Democracy, Development, Demography, and Diaspora and took note of Nigerian ideas to incorporate U.S. contributions to meeting these goals; noted that in FY 2023, U.S. development, humanitarian, and security assistance to Nigeria approached $1 billion annually.

a5880.speaker: Kurt M. Campbell, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
a5880.speech: Invited Foreign Minister Tuggar to meet Secretary Blinken in Washington at a date to be determined.

a5880.speaker: United States
a5880.speech: Announced a planned visit by the President's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement to Nigeria in July; the U.S. delegation also discussed a major symposium in Washington, D.C., in October to bring together American and Nigerian technology leaders, shared perspectives on emerging technologies and announced plans for a U.S. government-funded artificial intelligence (AI) conference in Lagos later this year.

a5880.speaker: Both sides (U.S. and Nigeria)
a5880.speech: Welcomed constructive comments from Nigerian and African businesses on the operating environment and discussed the importance of transparency and predictability for investors in Nigeria; reiterated their intent to take steps to expand trade and investment ties and shared an understanding that expanding ties offered the potential to support sustainable and inclusive economic growth and job creation in both countries.

a5880.speaker: Both governments (U.S. and Nigeria)
a5880.speech: Stressed their commitment to the overarching goals of the Biden-Harris Administration's Digital Transformation with Africa (DTA) initiative and expressed interest in deepening cooperation in strengthening Nigeria's digital economy through a structured forum for regular multi-stakeholder engagement every three months; shared their intent to strengthen bilateral space cooperation.

a5880.speaker: United States
a5880.speech: Commended Nigeria's ambitions to increase information and communications technology infrastructure and leverage opportunities to expand cooperation on emerging technologies development, such as AI.

a5880.speaker: United States
a5880.speech: Highlighted the importance of Nigeria removing import prohibitions and reducing high tariffs on a wide array of agricultural products to help address food insecurity and food price inflation; emphasised its engagement in improving food security and strengthening agricultural productivity, both globally and in Nigeria, including a new $75 million investment by the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) in Indorama's third urea-ammonia fertilizer facility in Port Harcourt, and announced its Global Food Security Strategy for Nigeria launched in March.

a5880.speaker: U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID)
a5880.speech: Shared a $50 million five-year Water for the World country plan for Nigeria approved in July 2023.

a5880.speaker: Nigeria
a5880.speech: Expressed its desire to increase African exports to the United States, and looks forward to further engagement with the U.S. government on the Blue Dot Network.

a5880.speaker: United States
a5880.speech: Reaffirmed its commitment to Nigeria's development and pledged efforts to facilitate Nigeria's use of trade opportunities; highlighted that Power Africa, working with Congress, intends to support a new, five-year, $90 million program to support on and off-grid development.

a5880.speaker: Both governments (U.S. and Nigeria)
a5880.speech: Recognising the threat of climate change, reaffirmed that they are committed to collaborating on and strengthening existing workstreams under the Net Zero World (NZW) Initiative, deploying renewable energy to reduce emissions and expanding electricity access, and rapidly reducing methane emissions and gas flaring to achieve the goal of the Global Methane Pledge; both sides look forward to the launch of the Clean Energy Alliance of Nigeria.

a6100.speaker: Algeria (Algerian government)
a6100.speech: Says it has always supported the independence movements of the Maghreb, notably the Polisario Front, out of humanitarian concern.

a6100.speaker: Professor Ibrahim Ndiaye, expert on the Committee in charge of implementing the National Programme of Education in Values
a6100.speech: Saw correctly in indicating that the Malian is characterised, on the one hand, by five cardinal values: humanity, empathy, the obligation to transmit human values to future generations, a sense of honour, and the acceptance of difference and otherness, at the societal, human and cultural level. And on the other hand, by five inviolable principles linked to the country itself: a Mali that is indivisible, inalienable, non-mortgageable, that no one may dispose of as private property, and imperishable.

a6100.speaker: Amadou Hampate Ba, Malian writer
a6100.speech: Said: "If you try too hard to throw away a frog that disgusts you, it ends up falling into a good pond."

a6163.speaker: Diplomats posted in Washington (unnamed)
a6163.speech: For the diplomats posted there, it is an unprecedented diplomatic success, since tradition had assigned to the State Department the competence for this type of partnership.

a6277.speaker: Letšeng Diamonds (press release)
a6277.speech: Says the mine is curtailing its waste mining activities as part of a broader cost-cutting strategy among measures aimed at conserving cash, protecting shareholder value, and ensuring the sustainability of operations ; “Considering the prolonged weakness in global diamond prices, compounded by a weak US dollar and ongoing US tariff uncertainties, Letšeng has implemented decisive measures to conserve cash and protect shareholder value” ; “While the company has met its production targets, it has not been immune to the sustained pressure on rough diamond prices” ; indicated that it has comprehensively reviewed its short-term mine plan and base operations to significantly reduce operational expenditure, and said both its treatment plants will continue to operate at existing volumes ; “As for waste mining volumes in both the main and satellite pits, they have been reduced to a minimum for an initial 12-month period, without compromising the long-term life-of-mine plan” ; “The company regrets that an approximately 20 percent workforce reduction may be necessary to align with the scaled-back waste mining operations and other required operational adjustments” ; stated that engagements with employees and relevant stakeholders have commenced and will continue to ensure that the rationalisation process is handled responsibly and transparently; assured shareholders that it remains committed to its long-term strategy and is confident that the measures being implemented will better position the company for a strong recovery once market conditions improve ; “The company will continue to monitor market developments closely and provide further updates.”

a6435.speaker: Saudi Press Agency
a6435.speech: Reported that Saudi Arabia and Ukraine issued a joint declaration on Tuesday following Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's visit to the Kingdom.

a6435.speaker: Saudi Arabia (joint declaration)
a6435.speech: Expressed hope that the efforts would result in ending the crisis in Ukraine in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter, including respect for the principles of sovereignty and internationally recognized borders.

a6435.speaker: Kyiv / the Ukrainian side
a6435.speech: Welcomed Riyadh's efforts to host the talks between Ukraine and the United States ; expressed its gratitude for the humanitarian and development aid provided by the Kingdom to Ukraine.

a6435.speaker: Saudi Arabia and Ukraine (joint declaration)
a6435.speech: In their joint declaration, the Kingdom and Ukraine also welcomed the strength of their economic ties and the importance of working together to expand the volume of trade between the two countries ; welcomed the re-establishment of the joint Saudi-Ukrainian Business Council in 2025 ; affirmed their determination to strengthen investment relations by establishing promising economic and investment partnerships ; discussed the latest developments and exchanged views on questions of common interest at the regional and international levels.

a6591.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a6591.speech: Praised the efforts made by the African Development Bank Group to help Africa feed itself and feed the rest of the world: "The African Development Bank is making the necessary investments in sustainable production in a smart and efficient manner, and, with its AfricaRice programme, it is maximising harvests and producing crops capable of withstanding climate change," he said, pleased with the positive and inspiring impact of the bank's initiatives and just as convinced as the US public administration that there was enormous investment potential in the production of climate-resilient and highly nutritious crops, including some of Africa's neglected traditional foods ; expressed his admiration for the AfricaRice results.

a6591.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6591.speech: Underlined the lasting impact of American investments in the Bank's operations, which align with Africa's shared priorities; said Secretary of State Blinken's visit is historic and gives tremendous momentum to the institution's work to feed Africa: "I salute Secretary of State Blinken's strong leadership and his commitment to food security, and I look forward to working closely with him and the American government to advance our joint efforts to help Africa feed itself and to contribute to feeding the world." He thanked the United States for its support to the bank group's key agricultural initiatives and said he was delighted by the partnership between the two sides.

a6591.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a6591.speech: Also welcomed the new 9.5 million dollar grant intended to support the Technologies for African Agricultural Transformation (TAAT) initiative led by his institution.

a6591.speaker: African Development Bank website (source cited)
a6591.speech: Reported Adesina's remarks on the historic nature of Blinken's visit, according to the African Development Bank's website.

a6745.speaker: FAO and IGAD (joint report)
a6745.speech: According to a report published on Monday by the FAO and IGAD, in June 2025 more than 88 million people in East and Central Africa were facing acute food insecurity requiring urgent humanitarian assistance; the report, drawn up jointly by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development, reveals that 57.1 million of these people live in seven of IGAD's eight member states: Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, South Sudan and Uganda.

a6745.speaker: FAO and IGAD (the two agencies)
a6745.speech: "Acute food insecurity levels remain alarming in the region, particularly with the current or imminent lean seasons aggravating the effects of conflict, climate hazards and macroeconomic pressures," the two agencies warn.

a6745.speaker: FAO-IGAD report
a6745.speech: The report indicates that at the end of June, 23.8 million people had been forcibly displaced in the region, including 18 million internally displaced persons (IDPs) and 5.8 million refugees or asylum seekers; Sudan alone accounts for more than half of the internally displaced, with 10.1 million people, of whom 7.7 million fled their homes after the outbreak of the current conflict.

a6754.speaker: Pentagon officials
a6754.speech: In late August, gathered European diplomats and delivered a blunt warning: U.S. security assistance to Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia would be scaled back, and the three NATO members on Russia's border must prepare to rely less on Washington.

a6754.speaker: David Baker, senior Pentagon official
a6754.speech: Drove the point home that under President Donald Trump, the U.S. military would be focusing inward, prioritizing homeland defense.

a6754.speaker: European diplomats (unnamed)
a6754.speech: Some worried the shift would embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin ; once buoyed by Trump's summer of engagement, are increasingly fatigued by his volatility and warn that a softer U.S. line risks encouraging more aggressive Russian behavior.

a6754.speaker: Estonia (government)
a6754.speech: Reported that Russian MiG-31 jets violated its airspace for about 10 minutes before being intercepted by Italian F-35s.

a6754.speaker: Poland (government)
a6754.speech: Said Russian jets buzzed an oil platform, following recent drone incursions.

a6754.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6754.speech: On the Russian incursions: after several hours, warned the Estonia incident could spell "big trouble"; following last week's drone episode in Poland, he had only posted cryptically on Truth Social: "Here we go!"

a6754.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6754.speech: On allied burden-sharing: at one tense call with European leaders, he accused them of expecting the U.S. to "bail them out" while still funding Russia's war machine through oil purchases; days later, he demanded the EU slap 100% tariffs on China and India for buying Russian oil, calling it a precondition for U.S. action. He campaigned on the argument that America was militarily overstretched.

a6754.speaker: Aaron David Miller, veteran diplomat and analyst at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
a6754.speech: Said Trump may simply have concluded that the conflicts are more intractable than he had hoped: "He's not interested in doing anything unless he sees that the expenditure of effort and political capital will be worth the return."

a6754.speaker: Alex Plitsas, senior fellow at the Atlantic Council
a6754.speech: "The more America steps back, the more provocative Putin becomes - he senses weakness and division in Europe."

a6754.speaker: Baltic states
a6754.speech: Pleaded with Washington to reverse the aid cuts.

a6754.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a6754.speech: Insisted: "Many of our European allies are among the world's wealthiest countries. They are fully capable of funding these programs if they choose."

a6759.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6759.speech: Vowed to cut off all future funding to South Africa, citing concerns over "land expropriation and alleged discriminatory treatment" of some residents, particularly foreigners in the country; in a post shared on his Truth Social on Sunday he condemned the situation, stating that the country is "confiscating land, and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY", and accused the "Radical Left Media" of ignoring the issue, which he described as a "massive Human Rights VIOLATION": "South Africa is confiscating land, and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY. It is a bad situation that the Radical Left Media doesn't want to so much as mention. A massive Human Rights VIOLATION, at a minimum, is happening for all to see. The United States won't stand for it, we will act. Also, I will be cutting off all future funding to South Africa until a full investigation of this situation has been completed."

a6759.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a6759.speech: In a statement issued on Monday morning, said his country is a constitutional democracy rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality; clarified that his government has not confiscated any land as claimed by Donald Trump; said the recently adopted Expropriation Act is a constitutionally mandated process aimed at ensuring public access to land in an equitable and just manner; noted that expropriation laws are not unique to South Africa; and expressed willingness to engage with the Trump administration: "South Africa is a constitutional democracy that is deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality. The South African government has not confiscated any land. The recently adopted Expropriation Act is not a confiscation instrument, but a constitutionally mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner as guided by the constitution. South Africa, like the United States of America and other countries, has always had expropriation laws that balance the need for public usage of land and the protection of rights of property owners. We look forward to engaging with the Trump administration over our land reform policy and issues of bilateral interest. We are certain that out of those engagements, we will share a better and common understanding over these matters. The US remains a key strategic political and trade partner for South Africa. With the exception of PEPFAR Aid, which constitutes 17% of South Africa's HIV/Aids programme, there is no other funding that is received by South Africa from the United States."

a6851.speaker: Agriculture Export Policy (Government of India policy document)
a6851.speech: Outlines broad strategies for addressing supply chain challenges, promoting product diversification, and improving logistics and storage infrastructure, including cold chains, to reduce post-harvest losses.

a6959.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), October Regional Economic Outlook
a6959.speech: Says Malawi could lose up to nine percent of government revenues following a decline in foreign assistance this year, placing Malawi as the fourth worst impacted economy after Central African Republic, South Sudan and Niger, whose potential aid cuts could surpass 10 percent of government revenues during the year ; said the reductions are both in budgetary assistance and off-budget support, and that governments have sought to reallocate budgetary resources to cushion these losses, but have limited fiscal space or technical capacity to rebuild fragmented, externally managed aid delivery systems.

a6959.speaker: Christopher Mbukwa, Mzuzu University economist
a6959.speech: Observed that less external financial support increases financial strain for Malawi as around 25 percent of government revenue goes to paying debt. He said: "Reduced aid coupled with high debt servicing will limit spending which, in turn, stifles economic growth and deepens poverty. Largely, the reduced official development assistance [ODA] flows will impact foreign exchange availability, which has been the reason why prices of key commodities such as fertiliser and fuel have remained high for an average Malawian."

a6959.speaker: Published United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) data
a6959.speech: Show that between 2017 and 2023, ODA has remained the largest external inflow, averaging $1.6 billion (about K2.8 trillion) compared to foreign direct investment, averaging $144 million (about K252 billion) and remittances at an average of $219 million (K383 billion).

a6959.speaker: United Nations
a6959.speech: In relative terms, ODA flows to Malawi constituted 82 percent of total external inflows in 2023, compared to FDI at 10 percent and remittances at eight percent, according to the UN.

a6959.speaker: Pamela Coke-Hamilton, International Trade Centre executive director
a6959.speech: Said ODA cuts that governments have announced in 2025 could amount to between a nine and 17 percent drop from last year's ODA levels, raising concerns over the stability of the international trading system.

a6959.speaker: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning and Development (Malawi)
a6959.speech: Projected the financing of the national budget through tax revenues to increase to 53.6 percent in 2025/26 fiscal year as grant financing will reduce to 14.2 percent.

a7051.speaker: Pre-print modelling study led by Dr. Jack Stone (University of Bristol)
a7051.speech: Warns that HIV incidence and related deaths in sub-Saharan Africa could significantly increase following the suspension of funding for Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) under PEPFAR. According to the study, the funding halt could lead to approximately 6,671 additional HIV acquisitions within a year and 3,617 more over the subsequent five years; more than 2,900 of the additional infections could occur among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men, while more than 2,000 could be among female sex workers. The research also suggests that increases in HIV acquisition will exceed 5 percent among key populations in several countries, including men who have sex with men in eight countries, people who inject drugs in two countries, transgender women in five countries, and female sex workers in six countries.

a7051.speaker: Dr. Jack Stone, Associate Professor in Infectious Disease Mathematical Modelling, University of Bristol
a7051.speech: “Ceasing PEPFAR’s funding for PrEP in sub-Saharan Africa will remove approximately 700,000 individuals from using oral PrEP. If this continued for one year, then 10,000 additional infections could occur over the next five years, with many of these infections being among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men and female sex workers,” said Dr. Jack Stone. “It is crucial that funding is found to continue and expand PrEP services in sub-Saharan Africa.”

a7051.speaker: Prof. Kenneth Ngure, President-Elect of the International AIDS Society (IAS)
a7051.speech: Noted that the study illustrates the real-world consequences of abrupt funding cuts. “This study and others to be discussed at the conference offer real-world insights into how sudden funding cuts are impacting vulnerable populations and the impact they could cause in the future,” he said. Prof. Ngure added that the cuts have been deeply felt across the African continent—not just by the millions of people depending on HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services—but also by the researchers and healthcare professionals working to end the pandemic. He noted that many clinical trials now face the risk of stalling due to the financial uncertainty.

a7077.speaker: Caroline Kautsire, United States-based Malawian writer and mentor
a7077.speech: Said yesterday that she realised there was a lot she could contribute to the lives of young Malawian girls and boys, hence bringing the scholarship; said her project was about responding to Malawi's need for young girls and boys to have access to educational pathways: “After a successful book tour in Malawi in 2024, when I raised funds and donated food, books and school materials to 10 institutions, I decided to focus on the scholarship.”

a7077.speaker: Caroline Kautsire, United States-based Malawian writer and mentor
a7077.speech: Said she could not do it alone, hence she created a GoFundMe page as one way of raising funds to make the scholarships available.

a7077.speaker: Caroline Kautsire, United States-based Malawian writer and mentor
a7077.speech: “This project will help students with both their tuition and upkeep funds. The identification of deserving students will be done through the selected school's bursary committees. The tuition money will be directly paid into the school accounts, with the upkeep money given directly to the students” ; further said the programme would help students in secondary school classes, with much focus on senior classes, which she indicated are often neglected by people and institutions.

a7181.speaker: Tanzania Investment and Special Economic Zones Authority (TISEZA)
a7181.speech: has announced that the regions of Dar es Salaam, Pwani, and Arusha have continued to lead in attracting new investment projects between July and September 2025.

a7181.speaker: Gilead Teri, TISEZA Director General
a7181.speech: Speaking to journalists while presenting the authority's first-quarter report, said the institution successfully registered 201 investment projects worth TSh 6.18 trillion, expected to create 20,800 jobs for Tanzanians and drive technological and economic growth nationwide.

a7181.speaker: Gilead Teri, TISEZA Director General
a7181.speech: Noted that during the July-September period, the sectors attracting the largest investments were manufacturing, commercial real estate development, and transportation. Out of the 201 projects, 74 were registered by local investors, representing 35 percent of the total - an increase from 27 percent in the same period last year.

a7181.speaker: Gilead Teri, TISEZA Director General
a7181.speech: He further revealed that the United Arab Emirates, China, and India topped the list of countries contributing foreign direct investment during the quarter, demonstrating growing global confidence in Tanzania's investment climate.

a7181.speaker: Gilead Teri, TISEZA Director General
a7181.speech: “Despite being in an election period, the pace of investment has not slowed down,” said Mr. Teri. “Tanzania remains a safe and reliable destination for investors—even during election seasons.”

a7190.speaker: Anne Witkowsky, US Assistant Secretary of State for Conflict and Stabilisation Operations
a7190.speech: noted that the CSSM project marked an important step forward in its partnership with Ghana as they worked together to enhance resilience and security across coastal West Africa in the face of regional threats, as Ghana stood out as a leader in the region and the “United States is proud to support the country's security efforts”.

a7190.speaker: Anne Witkowsky, US Assistant Secretary of State for Conflict and Stabilisation Operations
a7190.speech: The CSSM, according to her, was part of a broader US Strategy to Prevent Conflict and Promote Stability (SPCPS) in coastal West Africa and beyond and reiterated that through the strategy, the US was seeking to enhance social cohesion, improve government responsiveness and support security. “Through these initiatives, we aim to create lasting impacts that contribute to a more secure and resilient Ghana and the region. When Africa succeeds, the world succeeds,” Ms Witkowsky said, further emphasising the importance of CSSM and the broader US commitment to promoting stability and preventing violent extremism in West Africa.

a7284.speaker: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief
a7284.speech: Said 144 people had been killed, with 732 confirmed injured, but warned the toll was "likely to rise" ; "In some places, some buildings collapsed," he said in a televised speech, after visiting a hospital in the capital Naypyidaw.

a7284.speaker: Min Aung Hlaing, Myanmar junta chief
a7284.speech: Issued a rare plea for international aid: "I would like to invite any country, any organisation, or anyone in Myanmar to come and help. Thank you." ; urged massive relief efforts in the wake of the disaster and said he had "opened all ways for foreign aid."

a7284.speaker: World Health Organization
a7284.speech: Described the quake as a "very, very big threat to life and health."

a7284.speaker: World Health Organization
a7284.speech: Said it was mobilising its logistics hub in Dubai to prepare trauma injury supplies.

a7284.speaker: An official at a major hospital in Naypyidaw (unnamed)
a7284.speech: Described it as a "mass casualty area" with medics treating the wounded outside.

a7284.speaker: A doctor (unnamed), Naypyidaw hospital
a7284.speech: Told AFP: "I haven't seen (something) like this before. We are trying to handle the situation. I'm so exhausted now."

a7284.speaker: A resident of Mandalay (unnamed)
a7284.speech: Reached by phone, told AFP that a hospital and a hotel had been destroyed, among other buildings, and said the city was badly lacking in rescue personnel.

a7284.speaker: Anutin Charnvirakul, Thai Interior Minister
a7284.speech: Said eight dead bodies have been recovered and, with between 90 and 110 people unaccounted for, the toll is expected to rise: "We see several dead bodies under the rubble. We will take time to bring the bodies out to avoid any further collapses," he told reporters.

a7284.speaker: Worapat Sukthai, deputy police chief of Bang Sue district
a7284.speech: Told AFP: "I heard people calling for help, saying 'help me'."

a7284.speaker: Paetongtarn Shinawatra, Thai Prime Minister
a7284.speech: Visiting the site, said "every building" in Bangkok would need to be inspected for safety.

a7284.speaker: Bangkok city authorities
a7284.speech: Said parks would stay open overnight for those unable to sleep at home.

a7284.speaker: Sai, 76, resident of Chiang Mai
a7284.speech: "This is the strongest tremor I've experienced in my life."

a7284.speaker: India, France and the European Union
Pope Francis
a7284.speech: Said he was "deeply saddened by the loss of life and widespread devastation" in a telegram published by the Vatican.

a7284.speaker: United States Geological Survey (USGS)
a7284.speech: According to the USGS, six strong quakes of 7.0 magnitude or more struck between 1930 and 1956 near the Sagaing Fault, which runs north to south through the centre of Myanmar.
